afd.text:
000
FXUS65 KPSR 222010
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
110 PM MST Tue Sep 22 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Rain chances return to portions of eastern Arizona with most 
activity focused over foothill and high terrain areas.

- Best chances for lower desert rainfall will occur Wednesday and 
Thursday, though most activity should remain to the north and east 
of the Phoenix metro.

- Near to slightly above normal temperatures will persist over the 
next several days. 
  
&&

.SHORT TERM /Today through Thursday/...
As one vorticity center lifts northeast through the Great Basin, a 
lingering, elongated trough remains across the SW Conus extending 
south of the Baja peninsula. Per WV imagery, several vorticity 
centers are embedded in this weak southerly flow and will stream 
north over the next 72 hours periodically enhancing ascent structure 
as well as importing marginally better moisture poleward. The first 
such feature currently over Sonora will progress through eastern 
Arizona later today while a more defined circulation center over the 
southern Baja ejects through central New Mexico Wednesday. A final 
piece of energy incorporating the entire trough base and full extent 
of cyclonic influence will surge through central Arizona Thursday 
afternoon/evening potentially bringing the greatest short term 
impacts to the local forecast area.

Objective analysis indicates a pool of 10 g/kg mixing ratios across 
SE Arizona early this afternoon with a marked gradient towards under 
6 g/kg across the Phoenix metro. This has confined the area of 
instability largely outside the CWA though an increasing synoptic 
pressure gradient amplified by cool outflow will continue to enhance 
easterly boundary layer flow such that increasing shallow moisture 
should slosh westward over the next 24 hours. Forecast confidence is 
moderate regarding scattered showers and a couple embedded storms 
moving into southern Gila County this evening, albeit with low 
instability limiting the areal and temporal extent. Easterly winds 
should be invigorated by this activity which could conceivably 
result in some lofted dust into lower elevations, however even among 
the most aggressive high resolution models, a sudden surge and/or 
prolonged instance of gusty winds appears unlikely reducing the 
threat for dense dust. 

Global and HREF members agree that a well defined circulation center 
will propagate from the northern Mexico through western/central New 
Mexico Wednesday. This will place the eastern portions of the CWA 
within a deformation zone west of the circulation center with the 
expectation of thicker mid/high clouds and persistent showers 
hampering insolation. However, with better boundary layer moisture 
in place (~10 g/kg mixing ratios), clearing over mountains west of 
the deformation band should help realize MLCape 1000-1500 J/kg. 
Northeast steering flow should direct storms and outflow along the 
Mogollon rim towards the Phoenix metro, however CinH around 50 J/kg 
will need to be breached. Multiple colliding outflow boundaries 
necessary to achieve lower elevation storms are certainly possible, 
however there is only marginal support for this outcome among the 
full model suite and have maintained relatively low POPs. 

The main basal shortwave will pass directly into south-central 
Arizona Thursday with the full cyclonic curvature region and strong 
ascent signal juxtaposed with modest instability. Similar to 
Wednesday, lower elevation moisture levels may be too low to support 
more than isolated thunderstorm formation, however ascent structure 
will be far more conducive than Wednesday. Given this strong lift 
and DCape in excess of 1500 J/kg, models have been consistent in 
advertising at least 1 strong outflow boundary surging through the 
Arizona lower deserts. Colliding boundaries may be sufficient 
towards additional development in lower deserts, and pattern 
recognition and model evidence indicates this potential may skip 
over the Phoenix metro towards western Arizona, though have 
increased POPs marginally over the initialized NBM. Regardless, 
signals continue to show the possibility of an organized expansive 
and long duration blowing dust event. 

&&

.LONG TERM /Friday through Tuesday/... 
Late in the week, shortwave energy will have ejected northeast and 
become absorbed into the stronger westerly flow over the plains. In 
its wake, deep quasi-zonal westerly flow will gradually scour away 
moisture such that PWATS fall below 1" and boundary layer mixing 
ratios under 9 g/kg by Friday afternoon. A period of shortwave 
ridging through the first half of the weekend will also impose 
expansive synoptic scale subsidence such that only the most 
susceptible high terrain locations would support brief afternoon 
deep convection. In fact, instability and ascent parameters are so 
poor Saturday that NBM POPs are essentially under 5% across the 
entire region. 

Forecast confidence deteriorates significantly next week due 
uncertainties in a progressive westerly wave and potential 
interaction with tropical moisture. Ensemble members are in good 
agreement that a shortwave will deepen near the California coast 
early next week, then rapidly propagate through the intermountain 
West during the first half of the week. However, there is 
substantial differences in depth and timing of this feature, which 
will be crucial in determining the ability to tap deep, tropical 
moisture and resulting impacts across the SW Conus. In general, 
operational members are deeper and faster with this wave than the 
preponderance of NAEFS membership; and based on historical 
precedent, would favor a somewhat slower progression of the central 
cold core and trough axis though intensity towards the deeper 
solutions is preferred. While conceptually a slower, deeper outcome 
would favor drawing the full brunt of remnant tropical circulation 
and associated moisture into the Southwest (akin to the latest 12Z 
GFS), the wide uncertainty in the actual location of the tropical 
system combined with disparity in the location and timing of the 
trough passage yields a large variation of possible outcomes. 
Nevertheless at the very least, ensembles hint at jet energy and 
sheared shortwave drawing midlevel moisture inland Sunday/Monday 
yielding scattered showers and storms. Thereafter because of the 
vast ensemble spread, mandated NBM POPs are essentially modest 
values spread over a prolonged period and offer minimal actionable 
details at this time. 

In term of temperatures, much like during the short term, not much 
fluctuation in day-to-day readings is expected to occur. Daily 
values will hover right around to just above normal, which 
translates to lower desert readings ranging between 94-105 degrees 
through the weekend. Overnight lows will be slightly more elevated 
compared to where they typically are for late September, likely an 
effect of lingering moisture and cloud cover (at least for some 
spots), with readings between 70-82 degrees. Meanwhile higher 
elevation conditions will be quite comfortable as most locations 
should be in the 80s, with perhaps a few spots touching the lower 
90s. Lows for these spots in the upper 50s to lower 70s will be 
common.  

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 1733Z. 

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT: 
Primary aviation impact will be the potential for VCSH/VCTS this 
afternoon/evening, and gusty outflows. A westerly shift this 
afternoon looks unlikely with a brief period of S-SSW cross winds 
before shifting back out out the SE for the remainder of the TAF 
period. Under 10% chances remains for SHRA/TSRA activity to develop 
in the metro, with activity expected to remain the the south and 
east of the terminals. The the main SE'rely outflow from the 
previous package has been shifted back a few hours now expected just 
past midnight tonight, however a few gusty periods may still develop 
this evening ahead of the main outflow. Gusts will likely be near 
20kts with low confidence of BLDU or reduced VIS. FEW-SCT clouds 
will be common through the afternoon with lowest bases around 8-10 
kft AGL. There will also be increasing high clouds (around 25 kft) 
through the period and should become BKN by this evening. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH: 
No major aviation impacts are anticipated through the next 24 hours 
with mostly clear skies. Winds will favor W/NW at both KIPL and 
KBLH, with wind speeds mostly staying below 10 kts and periods of 
light and variable winds.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Near to slightly above normal temperatures will prevail over the 
next several days, with minimal day-to-day fluctuations. Daily rain 
chances return for the high terrain through the end of the workweek 
with lower desert chances focused on Wednesday. MinRHs between 15-
30% will be common across the region through the start of the 
weekend, with even higher readings (35-50%) for the far eastern 
districts. MaxRHs will range from fair to good over the western and 
central districts, to good and excellent for the eastern districts 
into the weekend. Drier air by the weekend will lower RHs slightly, 
but they should remain above critical fire weather thresholds. 
Outside of any thunderstorm related outflows, winds will follow 
familiar diurnal trends with typical terrain induced afternoon gusts 
around 15-25 mph. 

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...None.
CA...None.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...18
LONG TERM...18/RW 
AVIATION...Ryan
FIRE WEATHER...RW
